title: bug: submit_plan's rail refusal sends a forbidden-pattern false positive or an unfitting required phrase to moe.propose_rail, but propose_rail resolves GLOBAL rails only in customRules, so that escape hatch can never lift a rail refusal and dies with an uncoded "Rail not found" Error
description:
Found by defect hunt #10 (task-49a2c07f, architect-1dd28c7c) on 2026-11-03, with a repro at HEAD 677d051a.

PROBLEM
- submit_plan refuses a plan whose text contains a globalRails.forbiddenPatterns entry or misses a globalRails.requiredPatterns entry (submitPlan.ts:433-438, then util/rails.ts:16-29).
- Its refusal, assertPlanRails (submitPlan.ts:194-206), names an escape hatch: "if this rail is genuinely wrong for task X (e.g., a forbidden pattern that's a false positive, or a required phrase that doesn't fit), call moe.propose_rail { …targetScope: "GLOBAL" | "EPIC" | "TASK"… }".
- The docs give the same advice: docs/MCP_SERVER.md:380, docs/roles/worker.reference.md:32 ("Use moe.propose_rail only when the rail itself is wrong (e.g. a forbiddenPatterns false positive …)") and docs/roles/governor.reference.md:129.
- propose_rail cannot reach either list that check enforces:
  - A GLOBAL MODIFY_RAIL/REMOVE_RAIL resolves currentValue in globalRails.customRules only (proposeRail.ts:59-64), and approval edits only customRules (StateManager.ts:1396-1418).
  - EPIC and TASK proposals edit epicRails and taskRails, which checkPlanRails never reads (util/rails.ts:31-34: only forbiddenPatterns and global requiredPatterns are enforced).
  - No other tool or /ws message writes forbiddenPatterns or requiredPatterns after init; they are only read (state/persistence.ts:100-101, util/rails.ts).
- So a false positive blocks the plan for good. The only remaining fix is hand-editing .moe/project.json, which CLAUDE.md forbids. On this board the forbidden patterns include "innerHTML", so the trap is reachable: a plan that removes an innerHTML sink has to name it.
- The refusal is also uncoded. findRailIndex throws a plain Error (state/railChange.ts:7-8), which McpAdapter.ts:329 sends as -32000 with no codeName. propose_rail's other refusals are coded (invalidInput/notFound at proposeRail.ts:39, :44, :48, :58).

EVIDENCE: repro at HEAD 677d051a, run in a git-archive snapshot outside the checkout
- Files: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-49a2c07f/me/zzHunt49a2_railEscape.test.ts, output in railEscape.out.
- Command: `cd packages/moe-daemon && NO_COLOR=1 npx vitest run src/tools/zzHunt49a2_railEscape.test.ts`
- (c1) passes: submit_plan refuses 'innerHTML' and its message names moe.propose_rail.
- (c2) passes: an approved TASK ADD_RAIL "innerHTML is allowed in this task" does not change submit_plan's verdict.
- (r1) GLOBAL REMOVE_RAIL with currentValue 'innerHTML' (a forbiddenPatterns entry): Expected "no error", Received "Error: Rail not found for proposal prop-4cf1f882…".
- (r2) GLOBAL REMOVE_RAIL with currentValue 'error handling' (a requiredPatterns entry): the same.
- (r3) a GLOBAL REMOVE_RAIL of a value that is in no list: a plain Error, not a MoeError.
- Result: Tests 3 failed | 2 passed (5).

FIX DIRECTION
- For targetScope GLOBAL with MODIFY_RAIL or REMOVE_RAIL, resolve currentValue across globalRails.customRules, forbiddenPatterns and requiredPatterns, using findRailIndex's exact-then-trimEnd matching per list.
  - Exactly one list must hold the value. None, or more than one, is a coded refusal that writes nothing.
  - Approval re-resolves the value the same way and edits that list.
  - ADD_RAIL GLOBAL keeps adding to customRules.
  - The proposal record shape does not change.
- Put the resolve-and-apply logic in state/railChange.ts. StateManager.ts is at 1493 of the 1500 lines stateModules.test.ts allows, so applyRailChange's GLOBAL branch must stay the same size or shrink.
- Make findRailIndex's two refusals coded MoeErrors (notFound / invalidInput). Keep the "Rail not found" and "Ambiguous rail match" text, which StateManager.test.ts:936 and proposeRail.test.ts:127 match.
- docs/MCP_SERVER.md's propose_rail section should say which GLOBAL lists a MODIFY or REMOVE reaches. 0adea941 holds that file at filing time, so it is not in this row's files. Add the sync only if lanes.js shows the file free when you plan; otherwise the governor files it.

FILES
- packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/proposeRail.ts
- packages/moe-daemon/src/state/railChange.ts
- packages/moe-daemon/src/state/StateManager.ts (applyRailChange's GLOBAL branch only)
- packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/proposeRail.globalPatterns.test.ts (new)
- None of these is held at filing time.

VERIFICATION
Run vitest in a snapshot or the task worktree, never in the shared checkout: `npx vitest run src/tools/proposeRail src/state/StateManager.test.ts src/state/stateModules.test.ts src/tools/submitPlan.test.ts`.
definitionOfDone: In the new proposeRail.globalPatterns.test.ts, GLOBAL REMOVE_RAIL and MODIFY_RAIL proposals succeed (PENDING) for a forbiddenPatterns entry and for a requiredPatterns entry. Approving each one removes or replaces exactly that entry in project.json, checked after a reload from disk, and the plan submit_plan refused before the approval is then accepted.

In the same file, a GLOBAL MODIFY/REMOVE whose currentValue is in no rail list, or in two lists, is refused with a MoeError (INVALID_INPUT or NOT_FOUND) whose message still contains "Rail not found" or "Ambiguous rail match", and nothing is written to .moe/proposals/.

implementationPlan.description:

(a) packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/proposeRail.ts
- Import `{ findRailIndex, resolveGlobalRail }`.
- Replace the `const rails = params.targetScope === 'GLOBAL' ? ... customRules ...` block and its `findRailIndex(rails, ...)` call with:
  - `if (params.targetScope === 'GLOBAL') resolveGlobalRail(state.project?.globalRails, params.currentValue, proposalId);`
  - `else findRailIndex(params.targetScope === 'EPIC' ? state.getEpic(task.epicId)?.epicRails || [] : task.taskRails || [], params.currentValue, proposalId);`
  - above them, a 2-line comment: a GLOBAL value may sit in customRules, forbiddenPatterns or requiredPatterns (the two lists submit_plan enforces), and exactly one list must hold it.
- Append to the currentValue inputSchema description: `. For GLOBAL it may be a customRules, forbiddenPatterns or requiredPatterns entry; exactly one of those lists must hold it`.
- Leave the record shape and every other check alone. ADD_RAIL GLOBAL still appends to customRules.
(b) packages/moe-daemon/src/state/StateManager.ts
- Change only the import (`import { applyGlobalRailChange, findRailIndex } from './railChange.js';`) and applyRailChange's GLOBAL branch (about :1396-1418). After the existing `if (!this.project) throw new Error('Project not loaded');` it becomes:
  - `const project = { ...this.project, globalRails: applyGlobalRailChange(this.project.globalRails, proposal), updatedAt: new Date().toISOString() };`
  - `await atomicWriteJsonAsync(path.join(this.moePath, 'project.json'), project);`
  - `this.project = project;`
  - with one comment line: "Written before it is adopted: a failed write leaves memory and the proposal unchanged."
- The order changes on purpose: today it assigns before writing, so a failed write left memory ahead of disk.
- EPIC/TASK branches and the top-of-function guard are untouched.
- StateManager.ts went from 1493 to 1476 lines in the dry run, under stateModules.test.ts's 1500 budget. Do not grow it elsewhere.

- propose_rail resolves before createProposal, so a refusal writes nothing to .moe/proposals/.
- Approval re-resolves inside applyGlobalRailChange before the write. A refusal propagates through approveProposal, which leaves the proposal PENDING, and the WS APPROVE_PROPOSAL handler forwards the message as before, now prefixed `[NOT_FOUND] ` or `[INVALID_INPUT] `.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: moe.propose_rail with targetScope GLOBAL and MODIFY_RAIL or REMOVE_RAIL resolves currentValue across globalRails.customRules, forbiddenPatterns and requiredPatterns, and accepts it (PENDING) when exactly one list holds it. Human approval re-resolves the value and edits exactly that entry of that list in project.json. That makes submit_plan's documented escape hatch work for a forbidden-pattern false positive or an unfitting required phrase. A value held by no list, or by two, is a coded MoeError refusal (NOT_FOUND / INVALID_INPUT) that writes nothing. ADD_RAIL GLOBAL still appends to customRules. findRailIndex's refusals become coded and keep their text.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Four designs were weighed.
(1) Chosen, as the row's fix direction says: resolve a GLOBAL MODIFY/REMOVE value across customRules, forbiddenPatterns and requiredPatterns. Exactly one list may hold it, and approval re-resolves and edits that list. The proposal record shape is unchanged.
(2) Rejected: a new targetScope (e.g. GLOBAL_PATTERN) or a `railList` field on the proposal. That changes the MCP contract and the stored record, and the epic rails forbid breaking either.
(3) Rejected: letting a TASK or EPIC rail override a global pattern in checkPlanRails. That is a new semantic and broader than the bug.
(4) Rejected: first-hit-wins across lists. It would silently edit the wrong list when the same text is both a custom rule and a pattern; refusing such a value as ambiguous is safer.
Follow-up, outside this row's fixed files: submitPlan.ts:194-206's refusal still offers targetScope "EPIC" | "TASK", which can never lift a rail refusal. The governor can file it.
The first submit of this very plan was refused: its fixture quoted one of this board's forbidden patterns. That is the trap this row fixes, so the fixture now uses 'console.log'.
